title: Kara-Khanids
capsule: The Kara-Khanid Khanate (also Qarakhanids) was the first Turkic dynasty to convert to Islam and to rule sedentary Iranian-speaking populations in Transoxiana, founded by Karluk tribal leaders in the mid-9th century following the breakup of the Uyghur Khaganate. Around 934, the ruler Satuq Bughra Khan's conversion to Islam was a decisive cultural turning point; the khanate conquered the Samanid capital Bukhara in 999 under Nasr I, absorbing Transoxiana's Persian-Islamic literary and administrative tradition while Turkicizing its ruling culture. The khanate is associated with Mahmud al-Kashgari's Diwan Lughat al-Turk (1072–74), the first systematic comparative dictionary of Turkic languages. Internal division into eastern and western halves around 1041 led to subordination under the Seljuks and later the Qara Khitai, and the western khanate fell to the Khwarazmian Empire in 1212.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Transoxianan territory (Fergana, Bukhara, Samarkand) is attested from administrative and numismatic records; the Tarim Basin and eastern extent depend more heavily on narrative sources and are geometrically approximate, particularly for the earlier period before the khanate's formal division.
